correctness.rationale: O'Hara's uniqueness theorem and reflection symmetry place the center on the altitude. Finch's accessible statement of Shibata's theorem says the three central-angle/subtriangle-area ratios are equal. Since their numerators sum to \(2\pi\) and denominators to the triangle area, the base subtriangle of area fraction \(q\) must subtend angle \(2\pi q\). Direct isosceles geometry gives the same angle as \(2\arctan(1/(\lambda q))\), hence \(\lambda q\tan(\pi q)=1\). The left side is strictly increasing in q on \((0,1/2)\), and implicit differentiation and elementary tangent expansions give the monotonicity and asymptotics. A fresh bisection check over \(\lambda=10^{-3},0.1,1,10,10^3\) reproduced the defining equation and both asymptotic regimes.

originality.rationale: The location equation is an implication-level specialization of prior results rather than a new theorem under the audit's strict originality rule. O'Hara supplies uniqueness of the relevant center for convex bodies, so reflection forces the isosceles center onto the symmetry altitude. Finch publicly records Shibata's all-triangle characterization \(\angle APB/|APB|=\angle BPC/|BPC|=\angle CPA/|CPA|\). On an isosceles triangle, substituting the altitude coordinate and the elementary area fraction immediately yields \(\lambda q\tan(\pi q)=1\). The monotonicity and endpoint asymptotics are routine one-variable consequences of that equation. Thus absence of the formula verbatim does not preserve originality.

final_claim: For every nondegenerate isosceles triangle \(T_{a,h}=\operatorname{conv}\{(-a,0),(a,0),(0,h)\}\), the planar illuminating center is \(P=(0,qh)\), where \(q\in(0,1/2)\) is uniquely determined by \(\lambda q\tan(\pi q)=1\) with \(\lambda=h/a\); moreover \(q\) decreases strictly with \(\lambda\) and has the stated flat and tall-triangle asymptotics.
limitations: Only the planar renormalized inverse-square illuminating center of isosceles triangles is treated.
The general center definition, uniqueness, and equal angle-to-area characterization are prior results.
The original Shibata manuscript remains inaccessible and is retained as an access risk.
